html:
The Tulalip Tribes are a federally recognized tribe of Puget Sound in Washington, formed by Snohomish, Snoqualmie, Duwamish, Skagit and other Coast Salish peoples, with their reservation on Tulalip Bay near Marysville.

Before the treaty, these peoples lived in villages along the rivers that run into the sound, fishing salmon, gathering shellfish and travelling by canoe. Their language is Lushootseed. In 1855 their leaders signed the Treaty of Point Elliott with Isaac Stevens, governor of Washington Territory, and the reservation was set aside for them. A government boarding school ran there for decades. Today the tribe runs its own businesses and courts and works to restore the salmon runs.
sum: The Tulalip Tribes are a federally recognized tribe of Puget Sound in Washington, formed by Snohomish, Snoqualmie, Duwamish, Skagit and other Coast Salish peoples, with their reservation on Tulalip Bay near Marysville.
